sample_data.method: Both. The bundled sample household (case PUB-01 from P10_prepaid_meter_public.json) loads automatically on open, converted programmatically (not retyped by hand) into src/lib/data.ts. A different case in the same published fixture shape can also be supplied at runtime, either by choosing a .json file or by pasting the JSON text directly, in the 'Load a different case' panel at the top of the page.
sample_data.reset_instructions: Click 'Reset to sample data (PUB-01)' in the 'Load a different case' panel (only shown once a custom case has been loaded), or simply reload the page — no data is written back to any file or server, so a reload always returns to the bundled sample.

problem_solving_method: Rebuilt the tariff as a pure function that splits a day's units across slab boundaries by cumulative monthly units, keeping the slab counter and the recharge/fixed-charge logic as two independently-tracked pieces of state so the 'a recharge never resets the slab counter' rule (constraint in the problem statement) can't accidentally leak between them. Built the day-by-day ledger, the two forecast functions (run-out date, top-up-to-a-date), and the habit comparison as separate pure functions with no DOM/React dependency, so all of them could be unit-tested headlessly before any UI was built. Verified the full six-month ledger three independent ways before trusting it: the TypeScript engine, a from-scratch Python re-implementation of the same tariff, and a real-Chromium screenshot of the rendered chart. One real bug was found this way (see known_limitations / README) and fixed with a regression test.

R1.evidence: src/lib/data.ts (bundled sample) and src/lib/caseLoader.ts + src/components/CaseLoaderCard.tsx (load any other case in the same shape). Sample case PUB-01 contains 181 consecutive daily readings (Jan-Jun 2026) including a light month (Jan/Feb), a heavy summer month (May/Jun), and a large recharge in the last week of a month (৳4,300 on 26 May) — visible on the 'Balance, rebuilt day by day' chart on first load.

R2.evidence: src/lib/engine.ts: rebuildLedger(). Charges each day's units at the slab the month's running total has reached (splitting a day across a slab boundary when it crosses one), resets the counter on the 1st of each calendar month independent of recharges, takes demand charge + meter rent once on the first recharge of the month, adds 5% VAT to energy. Rendered as the balance line + recharge markers in src/components/BalanceChart.tsx (item 2's required chart).

R3.evidence: src/lib/engine.ts: forecastRunOut() and forecastTopUp(). Shown in 'The family's two questions' section — src/components/RunOutCard.tsx (run-out date) and src/components/TopUpCard.tsx (top-up amount, with an interactive date picker, broken into base energy / higher-slab premium / fixed charges / VAT).

R4.evidence: src/lib/engine.ts: simulateHabit() and runComparison(). Shown in 'Two recharge habits, same three months, same electricity use' — src/components/HabitComparisonCard.tsx. Both habits run on identical daily consumption and the same calendar-month slab counter per R-16; the sample case happens to produce an equal result for both habits, which R-16 explicitly allows and the UI states plainly rather than fabricating a difference.

R5_bonus_slab_warning.evidence: src/components/SlabLadder.tsx — shows the current month's position on the slab ladder and warns when fewer than 30 units remain before the next slab, with the next slab's rate.

R6_bonus_paste_recharge_history.evidence: src/lib/engine.ts: parsePastedHistory() and buildActualComparison(); UI in src/components/RechargeCompareCard.tsx ('Check against your real meter'). Accepts pasted lines of date, recharge_amount, actual_balance; rebuilds the ledger against the pasted recharge history when provided, and diffs any pasted actual-balance checkpoints against the rebuilt balance.

R7_bonus_month_bill.evidence: src/components/MonthBillCard.tsx ('One month's bill, broken down') — any month in the loaded case's data, broken into units / energy / demand charge / meter rent / VAT / total, with a month picker.

major_design_decisions: Kept all tariff/ledger/forecast/comparison logic in src/lib/ as pure functions with zero DOM or React dependency, so the domain math could be unit-tested headlessly and independently of the UI framework.

Made the household a piece of application state rather than a hardcoded constant, and added a case loader (file upload or paste), specifically so the app can be re-run against a judge's own hidden test case in the same fixture shape, not only the bundled sample.

Chose React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind + Recharts for the UI layer: a conventional, widely-understood stack with no backend, so the whole submission is a static site that can be deployed to any static host with no server to configure or fail.

Every numeric string in the fixture format (e.g. "350.00") is parsed and validated explicitly in src/lib/caseLoader.ts rather than assumed, so a malformed or unusual hidden test case produces a clear error message instead of a wrong number or a blank page.
known_limitations: The 'check against your real meter' comparison tolerance for flagging a mismatch is a fixed ৳1 in the UI (src/components/RechargeCompareCard.tsx); it is not configurable.

No automated visual-regression test exercises the chart's exact pixel output; the chart's correctness was checked by inspecting rendered SVG path counts and real-Chromium screenshots during development, not by an automated pixel-diff test.

During development, an earlier version of forecastTopUp() checked whether a recharge happened strictly before 'today' in the same month (using '<') to decide whether a new hypothetical recharge would be the month's first; this missed a recharge landing exactly on 'today' itself. It was found, fixed ('<=' comparison), and covered by a named regression test in src/lib/engine.test.ts before this submission — it never affected the bundled sample case's displayed numbers, since that case's own first June recharge fell several days before 30 June.

ai_tools_used.used_for: Writing the tariff/ledger/forecast/comparison logic in src/lib/, the React UI components in src/components/, the Vitest test suites, and the case-loading/paste-history features.
ai_tools_used.how_output_was_verified: Every headline calculation (opening/closing balance, run-out date, top-up breakdown, habit-comparison totals) was cross-checked three independent ways: the shipped TypeScript engine, a from-scratch Python re-implementation of the same tariff rules written separately, and manual inspection of the rendered app in a real Chromium browser (not just unit tests) to confirm the displayed numbers matched. 57 automated tests (src/lib/*.test.ts) cover the tariff slab-splitting math, the monthly-reset and fixed-charge rules, the two forecasts, the habit comparison (including the R-16 equal-cost case), and the case loader's input validation; all 57 pass via `npm run test`.
